# Draft:Interwar Slovene Nationalism

----
Interwar Slovene nationalism
Slovene nationalism was developing in the 1920s and 1930s as an ideology that campaigned for the autonomy of Slovenia within Yugoslavia.
The monarchy
The Yugoslav monarchy often showed adversity towards Slovene nationalism. The mostly Serbian monarchy often banned certain political parties for being too nationalist or separatist
The Slovene peoples party
The Slovene People's Party was a political party in the late Austro-Hungarian period and interwar Yugoslavia. It was a highly Catholic party supporting Slovene nationalism and Christian democracy. The party supported Slovene autonomy within Yugoslavia, and despite tightly controlled elections, was popular within Slovenia. It was a Catholic, Christian-democratic party that supported Slovene national autonomy within Yugoslavia. According to Mulej in 2018 it was popular with 36% of Slovenes voting for the party in 1920, before 1929, when the Serbian controlled  Yugoslav dictatorship began.
